title: Gears and belts
prompt: A labelled principle teaching rig based on pages 36 and 37 compares an external spur-gear pair and a separate pair of belt pulleys. Drive turns each input and shows its mechanically connected output. Compare ratios swaps compatible gear or pulley pairs with visible tooth counts or diameters. Cross belt switches the flexible belt between open and crossed routing to compare output direction; this crossed-belt extension is an explicit teaching adaptation beyond the page's open-belt diagram. The spur pair reverses direction, the open belt preserves it, and the crossed belt reverses it. See-through shows meshing teeth, belt contact and shafts. Speed, direction and ideal torque ratios are overlays. Do not cross a chain or toothed timing belt.
blurb: A principle teaching rig compares gear and flat-belt ratios, with a crossed-belt teaching adaptation beyond the book diagram.
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / Gears and Belts

sourceScope.adaptation: Teaching rig; crossed flat belt is an explicit extension beyond the open-belt diagram.

idealizations: Rigid spur gears with coarse polygonal involute flanks
No friction, belt slip or elastic deformation
Compare ratios and Cross belt stop the rig and exchange matched components; these are teaching controls
Direction and ideal torque readouts are overlays, not anatomy
